events.source_name: US National Weather Service Active Alerts
events.summary:
Areas of fog, which was reducing visibility to generally 1 to 3
miles at most locations, was ongoing over the plains of Central
and North Central Montana. Localized reductions to near one
quarter of a mile are possible near the north and east slopes of
adjacent terrain. Travelers should be prepared for reductions in
visibility and the potential for slippery conditions, especially
on bridges and overpasses.

Slow down, allow extra time to reach your destination, and use
your low beam headlights when traveling through reduced
visibility.

events.source_name: US National Weather Service Active Alerts
events.summary:
...The Flood Warning continues for the following rivers in North
Carolina...

French Broad River At at Grove Bridge Rd in Blantyre affecting
Henderson and Transylvania Counties.

.Excessive runoff from widespread 4 to 6 inches of storm total
rainfall will maintain flooding along the French Broad River.

* WHAT...Minor flooding is occurring and minor flooding is forecast.

* WHERE...French Broad River at at Grove Bridge Rd in Blantyre.

* WHEN...Until late tonight.

* IMPACTS...At 17.0 feet, Minor Flooding continues.  Floodwaters
continue to inundate farmland between the French Broad River and
the old railroad bed. Floodwaters may inundate the shoulders of
River Road near the Big Willow Road intersection. Floodwaters
continue to impact boat access areas at Grove Bridge Rd. and Crab
Creek Rd.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 9:00 AM EDT Monday the stage was 17.0 feet.
- Bankfull stage is 15.0 feet.
- Recent Activity...The maximum river stage in the 24 hours ending
at 9:00 AM EDT Monday was 17.7 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to fall below flood stage late
this afternoon and continue falling gradually over the course of
the week.
- Minor Flood Stage is 16.0 feet.
- Flood History...This crest compares to a previous crest of 17.0
feet on 05/16/1976.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood

events.summary:
At 852 AM MDT, A flood wave was moving down the Paria River and
through Paria Canyon. At 430 AM the Paria River Gauge at US-89
indicated a rise of 3 feet as the flood wave passed, with an increase
in flow to 2200 CFS.

HAZARD...Life threatening flash flooding.

SOURCE...Gauges reported.

IMPACT...Life threatening flash flooding of creeks and streams, urban
areas, highways, streets and underpasses.

Some locations that will experience flash flooding include...
Paria River from just north of US-89 to the Utah/Arizona border
including Paria Canyon.

events.title: US National Weather Service Active Alerts
events.source_name: US National Weather Service Active Alerts
events.summary:
The Michigan Department of Environmental Quality has issued an Air
Quality Alert for Monday October 12, for elevated levels of
fine particulates (PM2.5) due to wildfire smoke. Localized pollutants
levels within those area may reach the Unhealthy for Sensitive
Groups with the the potential for Unhealthy.

The alert is in effect for the following Michigan Counties,

Menominee, Dickinson, Iron, Marquette, and Baraga.

It is recommended that, when possible, you avoid strenuous outdoor
activities, especially those with heart disease and respiratory
diseases such as asthma.

Monitor for symptoms such as wheezing, coughing, chest tightness,
dizziness, or burning in nose, throat, and eyes. Reduce or eliminate
activities that contribute to air pollution, such as outdoor
burning, and use of residential wood burning devices.

Keep windows closed overnight to prevent smoke from getting indoors
and, if possible, run central air conditioning with MERV-13 or
higher rated filters.

For further information, please see EPA's Air Now site for up-to-
date air quality data at https://www.airnow.gov

For further health information, please see MDHHS' Wildfire Smoke and
Your Health site at https://www.michigan.gov/mdhhs/safety-injury-
prev/environmental-health/your-health-and-wildfire-smoke.
